title:
VOLUME AND SURFACE AREA,
(VOLUME OF PRISMS AND CYLINDERS)
objective: LO: I can calculate the volume of prisms and cylinders using the formula V = area of cross-section times length.

content.text: The volume of a prism equals the area of its cross-section multiplied by its length. A cylinder is a circular prism, so its volume = πr²h.
Key formulae: Prism: V = A × l (A = cross-section area, l = length). Cylinder: V = πr²h. Volume is measured in cubic units (cm³, m³).

examples.expr: Triangular prism: V = ½ × b × h × l

examples.desc: volume uses cross-section area, not surface area
that is the curved surface area, not volume

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Volume of any prism = area of cross-section multiplied by the length (or height) of the prism.
key_idea.caption: A = area of the uniform cross-section, l = length of the prism

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – cuboid
modelled_examples.question: Find the volume of a cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm.
modelled_examples.explanation: A cuboid is a rectangular prism.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – cylinder
modelled_examples.question: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Round to 1 d.p.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – triangular prism
modelled_examples.question: Find the volume of a triangular prism with base 6 cm, height 4 cm, and length 15 cm.
modelled_examples.explanation: Find the triangle area first, then multiply by the length.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – trapezoidal prism
modelled_examples.question: A prism has a trapezium cross-section with parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm, height 4 cm, and length 12 cm.
modelled_examples.explanation: Use the trapezium formula for the cross-section.

items.statement: Volume of a prism = area of cross-section × length
V = πr²h requires the radius, not the diameter
Volume and surface area use the same formula
Volume is measured in cubic units such as cm³

problems.text: A cylindrical tank of radius 0.5 m and height 1.2 m is filled with water. The water is poured into a rectangular tank measuring 1 m by 0.8 m. What depth does the water reach? Give your answer to the nearest cm.

A triangular prism-shaped chocolate bar has a cross-section that is an equilateral triangle with side 4 cm. The bar is 18 cm long. If chocolate weighs 1.3 g per cm³, find the mass of the bar to the nearest gram.
